root_cause.text: The hugetlb file-folio migration path in `mm/migrate.c` released `i_mmap_rwsem` too early, so `remove_migration_ptes()` could reacquire `i_mmap_rwsem` while already holding `folio_lock`, violating the required lock order and creating an ABBA deadlock with `hugetlbfs_fallocate()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping)` from before `remove_migration_ptes()` to after it, and passes `RMP_LOCKED` into `remove_migration_ptes()` so the existing `i_mmap_lock` scope covers that call; the commit message explicitly says the migration path was “taking locks in the wrong order” and that `336bf30eb765` incorrectly removed this ordering for “both file & anon hugetlb pages” when it should have applied only to anon pages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Delay unlocking the mapping until after migration PTE cleanup and pass the appropriate lock flag to fix huge page migration handling.
intent_record.what: The call to `i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping)` was moved out of the inner `if (ttu & TTU_RMAP_LOCKED)` block and placed after `remove_migration_ptes()`. Also, the third argument to `remove_migration_ptes()` changed from a constant `0` to `ttu ? RMP_LOCKED : 0`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the mapping write lock is now held until after migration PTEs are removed, instead of being released earlier. The migration PTE removal helper also now receives a lock-state flag when `ttu` is nonzero, which changes how that helper treats the PTE removal path and can preserve the correct locking behavior during huge page migration.

commit 336bf30eb76580b579dc711ded5d599d905c0217
Author: Mike Kravetz <mike.kravetz@oracle.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 13 22:52:16 2020 -0800

    hugetlbfs: fix anon huge page migration race
    
    Qian Cai reported the following BUG in [1]
    
      LTP: starting move_pages12
      BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffffffffffffe0
      ...
      RIP: 0010:anon_vma_interval_tree_iter_first+0xa2/0x170 avc_start_pgoff at mm/interval_tree.c:63
      Call Trace:
        rmap_walk_anon+0x14
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the vulnerable path and the fix. Before the change, when `page_mapped(hpage)` was true, the code always did `mapping = hugetlb_page_mapping_lock_write(hpage);` and then `try_to_unmap(... TTU_RMAP_LOCKED);`, explicitly holding `i_mmap_rwsem` across the later `remove_migration_ptes()` call: `/* Leave mapping locked until after subsequent call to remove_migration_ptes() */` followed by `i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping);`. That matches the root cause of holding `i_mmap_rwsem` too early and risking lock inversion in migration. In the patched code, this is corrected: it introduces `if (!PageAnon(hpage)) { ... mapping_locked = true; ttu |= TTU_RMAP_LOCKED; }`, so anon huge pages no longer take `i_mmap_rwsem` or set `TTU_RMAP_LOCKED`. It also unlocks earlier only when needed (`if (mapping_locked) i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping);`) and calls `remove_migration_ptes(..., false)` instead of relying on a held mapping lock. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present in the pre-fix logic shown by the removed code, and the current commit body already contains the fix.
